requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1
requirements.summary: Confirmed appworker did not exist beforehand (cmd-e2c759251982465f), then created via useradd -m with uid/gid 1001 (cmd-5e23f203003c42b8), and getent passwd confirms the account both before and after restart (cmd-1583d6012bab4bac, cmd-345ba070c2db4e5f).

requirements.requirement: Limit appworker login sessions to 8,192 open files
requirements.summary: limits.d config sets soft/hard nofile 8192 (cmd-ebb399b234674f90) and a real login shell (su -l) shows ulimit -n = 8192 both before and after the restart (cmd-5f548d39803b478d, cmd-345ba070c2db4e5f).

requirements.requirement: Limit appworker login sessions to 256 processes
requirements.summary: limits.d config sets soft/hard nproc 256 (cmd-ebb399b234674f90) and a real login shell shows ulimit -u = 256 both before and after the restart (cmd-5f548d39803b478d, cmd-345ba070c2db4e5f).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task instruction are satisfied: the appworker account was created on node1, and its login sessions are limited to 8,192 open files and 256 processes via /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf, directly confirmed by ulimit values inside a real su -l login shell both before and after a full node restart. The independent provider-wide restart evidence protocol was also executed correctly and completely: a pre-restart boot_id (8660e8f0...) and healthy baseline were captured, a self-acknowledging reboot was issued, the node was observed briefly unreachable, and it came back with a new boot_id (656b844c...) with the account, config, and enforced limits all re-verified afterward. No unnecessary mutations or residue were introduced.
limitations: Evidence for the pre-restart baseline and restart transition relies on a single executor attempt's captured commands rather than an independently repeated observation; no contradictory or ambiguous evidence was found, but this is the only run examined.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 9 executor commands chronologically: existence/sudo check (read-only), useradd -m (required to satisfy task), limits.d file write (required), two login-shell verifications (read-only diagnostics), a self-acknowledging reboot plus polling for reachability (part of the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol, not the public task contract, but a bounded and clearly purposeful action), and post-restart re-verification (read-only). No unnecessary or unexplained mutations, no residue beyond the single required limits.d file, no failed services, no package-state damage, and the boot-identity/temp-file diffs in the lifecycle snapshots are simply artifacts of the legitimate restart (stale systemd-private tmp dirs from the old boot were replaced by new ones from the new boot), not executor residue.
